This Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, has been filed by the appellants / claimants for enhancement of the sum awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

Shortly stated, on 20.03.2019 at about 2.45 p.m. the deceased was driving the Hero Passion Pro Motor Cycle bearing Registration No.TN 46 P 5458.

At that time, one Toyoto Etios Car bearing Registration No.TN 46 M 4656 owned by the 1st respondent and insured with the 2nd respondent was driven by its driver, at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased vehicle and caused the accident.
At the time of accident, the deceased was 46 years old.
He was employed as driver in the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation Limited, Perambalur Depot and was drawing a monthly salary of Rs.25,000/-.

sentences.text: Accordingly Claim for compensation has been made by the legal heirs of the deceased.
3. The respondents alleged that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased.

Accordingly, the Claims Tribunal https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
12/01/2026 07:07:37 pm ) framed necessary issues and came to the conclusion that the accident took place as alleged and claimants are entitled to claim compensation.
A compensation of Rs.25,00,975/- was awarded by the Tribunalafter deducting 50% for the deceased's contributory negligence.
Aggrieved by this, the appellants / claimants are on appeal.

4. Mr. C. Vidhusan , the learned counsel for the appellants / claimants submits that the order of the Tribunal in fixing 50% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased is not based on any evidence and hence the same is liable to be set aside.
She would also contend that the tribunal failed to award consortium for the three minor children.
Hence, she prayed for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

5. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the 2 nd respondent / Insurance Company would submit that the learned Tribunal has deducted 50% as contributory negligence on the part of the deceased based on evidence.
Hence, fixing 50% contribution on the side of the deceased towards his negligence is factually and legally correct, which requires any interference by this Court.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 12/01/2026 07:07:37 pm )
6. Heard on both sides.
Records perused.
7. It is not in dispute that the FIR was registered against the deceased Chelladurai based on the complaint lodged by the driver of the offending vehicle.
No independent witness was examined on the side of the respondents to establish that the alleged accident took place solely on the negligent act of the deceased.
Moreover, the driver of the 1st respondent's vehicle had deposed that FIR was registered only at the instance of the Superintendent of Police.
Therefore, there is no rebuttable evidence on the side of the respondents that the alleged accident was not caused by the driver of the 1 st respondent's vehicle.
Under these circumstances, the quantum on the ground of contributory negligence is limited to 30% on the part of the deceased.
Further on a perusal of the impugned award it is found that no amount was awarded towards consortium for the minor children.
Hence, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded for each minor children.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal,
under various heads, is modified by this Court as follows:
